title: MZI A path-length difference is 79.94 um, intent is 100.0 +-0.5 um (20.06 um short)
evidence: Arms of MZI A run between ebeam_y_1550#6 (opt2 47.4,2.75 / opt3 47.4,-2.75) and ebeam_y_1550#7 (opt3 192.6,2.75 / opt2 192.6,-2.75). Short arm route_a_short: straight 47.4->192.6 at y=2.75, 145.20 um (incl. its 5 um Si Slab piece). Long arm route_a_long#9 (rv.instances): straights 10 + 34.264 (x=62.4, y -7.75..-42.014) + 105.2 (y=-47.014) + 34.264 (x=177.6) + 10, plus 4 bends of footprint 5 um, centre-line 7.852 um each (pi/2*5=7.854; my centre-line extraction of the bend polygons, work/intent/bends2.py). Long = 193.728 + 4*7.854 = 225.144 um; optical_net_geometry N12 gives 225.20 (area/width). dL_A = 225.14 - 145.20 = 79.94 um (79.99 by area). MZI B, built the same way, gives 60.34 um (in spec), so A's vertical legs are 10.03 um too short each (34.26 vs 44.29 needed).
impact: FSR = lambda^2/(n_g dL) with n_g = 4.18 (rv.modes, 500 nm strip): 7.19 nm instead of 5.75 nm (+25%). All fringe positions move; an n_g or dL extraction that assumes dL = 100 um is off by 20%. Error is 40x the +-0.5 um tolerance and there is no heater to tune it. MZI A does not deliver its specified filter response.
fix: Lengthen both vertical legs of route_a_long by 10.03 um (34.264 -> 44.292 um), i.e. move its bottom straight from y=-47.014 to y=-57.042; check with dL = 2*44.292 + 4*7.854 - 20 = 100.0 um.

title: Loopback input route (route_c_in) is 150 nm off axis at both ends: GC4 port and crossing opt2
category: intent: route meets port on axis
evidence: route_c_in#19 is one 500 nm Si rectangle x 0..115.2, y 507.90..508.40, centre y = 508.150 (rv.cell_shapes). The pins it joins are on y = 508.000: ebeam_gc_te1550#4.opt1 (0, 508.0) and ebeam_crossing4#18.opt2 (115.2, 508.0) (rv.extraction pin_xy). rv.cross_section either side of each joint: route centre +0.150, device centre 0.000, at x=0.05/-0.05 and at x=115.15/115.25. Mode-overlap loss for a 0.15 um side offset: rv.junction_loss(0.5,0.5,0.15) = 1.70 dB per joint; my own 1-D effective-index check gives 1.49 dB (work/intent/check_offset.py). The extraction and LVS still connect it, because the pieces overlap.
impact: Two offset joints in series: about 3.0 to 3.4 dB of unplanned loss on the loopback path (GC4 -> crossing -> GC5), plus some back-reflection. The loopback is the grating-coupler reference used to normalise MZI A and MZI B, so every normalised MZI spectrum is wrong by this amount. Critical by the intent (> 1 dB).
fix: Move route_c_in down by 0.150 um so its centre line is y = 508.000 from GC4 opt1 to crossing opt2.

title: GC3 is at y = 383.0, intent y = 381.0: grating-coupler pitch 129/125 um instead of 127 um
evidence: rv.instances: ebeam_gc_te1550#3 origin (0, 383.000), angle 0; the FbrTgt of GC3 is y 378.5..387.5 (centre 383.0). The other GCs: 0, 127.0, 254.0, 508.0, 635.1. Pitches GC0..GC5 = 127.0, 127.0, 129.0, 125.0, 127.1 um. route_b_out was drawn to meet GC3 at y=383 (its last straight y 382.75..383.25), so the layout is self-consistent and LVS passes.
impact: A rigid 127 um fibre array put on GC2 (MZI B input) places the GC3 fibre 2.0 um off the GC3 fibre target. Gaussian overlap with MFD 10.4 um (w0 = 5.2 um): exp(-(2.0/5.2)^2) = 0.86, about 0.64 dB extra loss on the MZI B output (about 0.32 dB if the array is centred between GC2 and GC3). Also the array cannot be optimal on GC0..GC5 at the same time.
fix: Move ebeam_gc_te1550#3 to (0, 381.0) and shorten the vertical leg of route_b_out by 2.0 um so it ends on y = 381.0.

title: GC5 is at y = 635.1, intent y = 635.0 (0.1 um): harmless
evidence: rv.instances: ebeam_gc_te1550#5 origin (0, 635.100). route_c_out follows it with a 1.411 um long s-bend (s_bend at x 198.589..200.0, y 635.0 -> 635.1; circular s-bend with 0.1 um offset over 1.411 um gives R = 5.0 um) and a straight on y = 635.1 that meets GC5 opt1 on axis (cross_section centre 0.000 either side of x = 0).
impact: Fibre offset 0.1 um: exp(-(0.1/5.2)^2) -> 0.002 dB. The R = 5 um s-bend adds about 0.004 um of path and negligible loss. No functional effect; reported as a harmless difference from the intent.
fix: Optional: move GC5 to y = 635.0 and replace the s-bend by a straight, for a clean 127 um pitch.

title: route_b_out (MZI B output to GC3) has two 90-degree bends of radius 2.0 um; intent is 5 um or more
evidence: route_b_out#17 sub-cells bend__DEGEJ4... at (260,254) angle 0 and (262,381) angle 90: footprint 2.25 x 2.25 um with a 0.5 um core, i.e. centre-line radius 2.0 um; centre-line length 3.140 um = pi/2 * 2.0 (area/width 3.147; work/intent/bends2.py). Every other bend on the chip has footprint 5.25 um and length 7.852 um (R = 5). Local Tidy3D mode solve (work/intent/bend_overlap2.py, rv._solve with bend_radius): R = 2 um bend mode n_eff 2.449, radiation 0.9 dB/cm (negligible), straight-to-bend overlap T = 0.991 -> 0.039 dB per joint, 0.079 dB per bend; R = 5 um gives 0.012 dB per bend.
impact: About 0.16 dB on the MZI B output path for the two bends (0.13 dB more than R = 5 um bends), each bend above the 0.05 dB unplanned-loss limit. Insertion loss only (outside the interferometer); no effect on fringe position. Small radius also raises sensitivity to width/etch variation and TM conversion.
fix: Redraw the two corners of route_b_out with R = 5 um bends (the vertical leg moves to x = 265, as in route_a_out).

title: Confirm twins-1: MZI A short arm core is on Si Slab for 5.0 um
evidence: Independent: rv.cross_section(61, 2.75, 0, ['Si','Si Slab']) -> Si none, Si Slab 0.50 um centred; (100, 2.75) -> Si 0.50 um. optical_net_geometry N11 layers {'Si': 70.1, 'Si Slab': 2.5}: 140.2 um on Si + 5.0 um on Slab = 145.2 um arm. rv.junction_loss(0.5, 0.5, layer2='Si Slab') = 0.97 dB per end. Intent: every route is the TE_1550_500 strip on Si.
impact: Agree high: about 1.9 dB or more in one MZI A arm (arm imbalance, extinction ratio limited to roughly 19 dB even before propagation loss in the slab section), > 1 dB on the MZI A path.
fix: Draw the 5 um piece on Si (1/0).

title: Confirm microscope-1 / twins-2: 0.5 um gap in MZI B short arm
evidence: Independent: rv.cross_section(137.4, 256.75, 0, ['Si','Si Slab']) -> nothing; (100, 256.75) -> Si 0.50 um. rv.extraction(): N8 = [ebeam_y_1550#12.opt2] and N10 = [ebeam_y_1550#13.opt3], each one pin; intent N8 needs them joined. rv.lvs() design_only includes this pair.
impact: Agree high: MZI B has effectively one arm; no useful fringes, several dB extra loss GC2 -> GC3.
fix: Close the gap (one continuous 500 nm straight from x 47.4 to 192.6 at y 256.75).

title: Confirm twins-4: route_a_in is 0.30 um wide over its full 32.6 um
evidence: Independent cuts rv.cross_section at x = 0.05, 16, 32.55 (y=0, dir 0): Si 0.300 um centred; GC0 side (x=-0.05) 0.531 um, Y-branch side (x=32.65) 0.500 um: abrupt steps. rv.junction_loss(0.5, 0.3) = 0.052 dB per step.
impact: Agree medium: about 0.1 dB plus extra scattering on the MZI A input; outside the interferometer, so no effect on dL or fringes.

title: Confirm twins-5: 2.0 um long 0.25 um neck in route_a_out at x=265, y=19.02..21.02
evidence: Independent: rv.cross_section(265, 20, 90, ['Si']) -> 0.250 um centred on x=265; rv.cell_shapes('route_a_out') piece [264.875, 19.024, 265.125, 21.024]. rv.junction_loss(0.5, 0.25) = 0.86 dB per step. The neck is short (2 um), so the two-step sum (1.7 dB) is an estimate; the light lost into radiation at the first step spreads well beyond the core within 2 um, so little of it is recaptured.
impact: Agree: roughly 1 to 1.7 dB on the MZI A output path; high by the 1 dB rule.
fix: Restore the 0.50 um width over y 19.024..21.024.

title: Confirm twins-6: route_b_out bends are R = 2.0 um (my intent-5 is the same defect)
evidence: Same geometry as intent-5 (posted by me before I saw twins-6; treat intent-5 as a duplicate of twins-6). My own local solve (work/intent/bend_overlap2.py): R = 2 um bend mode n_eff 2.449, k 2.6e-6, straight-to-bend overlap 0.039 dB per joint; R = 5 um: 0.006 dB per joint.
impact: Agree medium: about 0.16 dB on the MZI B output path; rule violation.

title: Confirm twins-9: route_b_in 5 nm off axis is harmless
evidence: Independent: rv.cross_section(0.05, 254, 0) and (32.55, 254, 0) -> route centre +0.005 um; device sides 0.000. rv.junction_loss(0.5, 0.5, 0.005) = 0.0019 dB per joint.

title: Confirm twins-10: crossing at 90 deg still gives a straight-through loopback; LVS pin-name mismatch only
evidence: Independent: union of ebeam_crossing4 Si vs the same rotated 90 deg about its origin: symmetric difference 0.0044 um^2 of 16.46 um^2 (work/intent/crossing_sym.py). In the cell frame opt1 = W, opt2 = N, opt3 = S, opt4 = E, so intent pairs (opt1, opt4) and layout pairs (opt2, opt3) are both through-pairs. Layout: GC4 -> opt2 (115.2, 508) -> opt3 (124.8, 508) -> GC5, terminators on the N and S arms, as the intent table says.
impact: None optically. The LVS against intent_nets.json fails on 4 crossing nets, so either rotate the crossing back to 0 deg or update the netlist before sign-off.
fix: Rotate ebeam_crossing4#18 to 0 deg (or accept and update intent_nets.json).

title: Confirm twins-3 (= intent-2) and correct intent-2: the PDK DRC does flag the route_c_in offset
evidence: rv.drc() (PDK deck): SiEPIC-1a markers at [-0.05,507.75,0.05,508.25] (GC4 pin) and [115.15,507.75,115.25,508.25] (crossing opt2 pin), plus Si_space [-0.069,508.25,0.0,508.322] (notch between the GC4 taper end and the shifted route). So intent-2 should read drc_or_lvs_flags_it = true (the extraction/LVS do not flag it; the DRC pin check does). The same SiEPIC-1a rule also marks both ends of route_a_in (twins-4, 0.30 um width) and of route_b_in (twins-9, 5 nm offset; also a 0.021 um Si_space notch at the GC2 joint).
impact: Unchanged: about 3 to 3.4 dB on the loopback.

title: Confirm twins-11: MZI B dL = 60.34 um, inside 60.0 +-0.5
evidence: route_b_long#15: straights 10 + 24.463 + 105.2 + 24.463 + 10 = 174.126 um + 4 bends x 7.854 um (R = 5) = 205.542 um; short arm 47.4 -> 192.6 = 145.2 um (geometric, ignoring the gap of microscope-1). dL_B = 60.342 um (+0.34 um, inside tolerance). FSR with n_g = 4.18: 9.52 nm vs 9.58 nm at 60.0 um.
impact: None (once the short-arm gap is closed).
